::: {#exr-miller-deriv-second-product}
#### Second derivative of a product

Find the second derivative of

$$f(x) = (x^4 + 3x^2 + 8)\cos x$$
:::

::: {#sol-miller-deriv-second-product}
From @exr-miller-deriv-product-poly-cos, the first derivative is:

$$f'(x) = (4x^3 + 6x)\cos x - (x^4 + 3x^2 + 8)\sin x$$

Differentiate each term via the product rule:

$$\ba
\dif{}{x}\sb{(4x^3 + 6x)\cos x} &= (12x^2 + 6)\cos x - (4x^3 + 6x)\sin x
\\
\dif{}{x}\sb{-(x^4 + 3x^2 + 8)\sin x} &= -(4x^3 + 6x)\sin x - (x^4 + 3x^2 + 8)\cos x
\ea$$

Combining and grouping like trigonometric terms:

$$\ba
f''(x) &= \sb{(12x^2 + 6) - (x^4 + 3x^2 + 8)}\cos x - 2(4x^3 + 6x)\sin x
\\
&= (-x^4 + 9x^2 - 2)\cos x - (8x^3 + 12x)\sin x
\ea$$
:::
